rationale: The construction is internally consistent (both legs high = demand-unbacked capex financed by dilution, expected negative), but it is essentially a recombination of two legs already tested in the archive (capex/sale escalation and the sstk-minus-internal-cash dilution term), so the incremental mechanism is modest and partly overlaps the known external-financing anomaly.

This is the fourth gate-swap on the identical maintenance-deviation leg (after retained-earnings, current-liability, and sales-productivity gates) and reuses the deleveraging leg from two prior signals, making it a cosmetic variant rather than a substantively different hypothesis.

Substituting an accumulated retained-earnings deficit (a stock-based funding-history state) for the prior flow-based cash-coverage gates is a defensible response to the diagnosed fmb/alpha divergence, though it is still the third pass at the same intangible-conversion leg and the RE/at gate partly proxies for known distress/RE-based valuation effects.

Goodwill creation in excess of cash acquisition outlays is a genuinely new construct (it effectively isolates stock-financed or premium-heavy deals, echoing but not duplicating the archive's goodwill-growth signal), but the measure is accounting-noisy since Δgdwl also absorbs impairments and aqc covers non-goodwill purchase price, so interpretation of the extremes is uncertain.

This is close to a linear combination of two well-documented published anomalies — inventory growth (Thomas–Zhang) with a negative sign and operating cash flow/accruals (Sloan) with a positive sign — scaled by assets, so it is more rediscovery than novel cross-theme interaction.

Intersecting two already-evaluated, capx-driven signals via MIN adds little independent information because the legs share the same numerator and are likely highly correlated, so any gain is more likely from tail-thinning and reduced coverage than from a new economic condition.
